etymologies.etymologyHTML: Clipping of brassiere, borrowed from French brassière, from Old French braciere (originally a lining inside armor to protect the arm, but later a garment), from Old French brace (“arm”), from Latin bracchia, plural of Latin bracchium (“forearm”), from Ancient Greek βραχίων (brakhíōn, “forearm”), from Proto-Hellenic *brəkʰús (“short”) (because the forearm is shorter than the upper arm), inherited from Proto-Indo-European *mréǵʰus.

definitions.definition: An item of clothing, usually underwear worn to support the breasts. [from 1920s]

quote.citation: 1968, Carl Ruhen, The Key Club, Sydney: Scripts, page 12:
quote.text: Her housecoat had fallen open. She was wearing only panties and bra, which did nothing to make her scrawny, wrinkled body appealing.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From bracket, referring to the notation introduced in 1939 by Paul Dirac.

definitions.definition: (physics) One of the two vectors in the standard notation for describing quantum states in quantum mechanics, the row vector; the other (column) vector being its complex conjugate, the ket.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: Representing a different pronunciation of bro (“brother”).

definitions.definition: (slang) Alternative form of bro; friend, mate
